name: Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER)
description: Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) in E. coli removes bulky DNA lesions including UV-induced cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPDs), 6-4 photoproducts, and chemical adducts. The UvrABC system performs damage recognition, dual incision, and excision of a 12-13 nucleotide oligomer containing the lesion. UvrA-UvrB complex scans DNA for helix distortions, UvrB verifies damage and remains bound, UvrA dissociates, UvrC catalyzes dual incisions (5' and 3' to lesion), UvrD helicase removes the excised fragment, DNA polymerase I fills the gap, and DNA ligase seals the nick. This flowchart illustrates the complete NER pathway from damage recognition through strand restoration, including both transcription-coupled and global genome repair sub-pathways.
scientificAccuracy: This flowchart is based on decades of biochemical and genetic studies of the E. coli UvrABC system. All protein components, recognition mechanisms, and catalytic steps have been validated against primary research including crystallographic structures. The model represents the paradigm for prokaryotic NER, a pathway essential for survival after UV exposure and conserved across bacteria.

    AL --> AM[UvrD Helicase Recognition]

    AR --> AS[Excised Fragment Release]
    AS --> AT[UvrB Dissociation]
    
    AT --> AU[Single-Strand Gap 12-13 nt]
    AU --> AV{Gap Filling Ready?}
    
    %% DNA Synthesis
    AV -->|3'-OH Present| AW[DNA Pol I Recognition]
    AV -->|End Processing Needed| AX[Additional Factors]
    
    AW --> AY[Pol I 5'-3' Polymerase]
    AY --> AZ[dNTP Incorporation]
    AZ --> BA[Processive Synthesis]
    BA --> BB[Gap Filled 12-13 nt]
    
    BB --> BC{Nick Remaining?}
    BC -->|Yes| BD[DNA Ligase Recognition]
    BC -->|No| BE[Unexpected State]
    
    %% Nick Sealing
    BD --> BF[NAD+ Ligase LigA]
    BF --> BG[Adenylate Transfer]
    BG --> BH[Phosphodiester Bond Formation]
    BH --> BI[Nick Sealed]
    
    BI --> BJ[Restored DNA Helix]
    BJ --> BK{Repair Verification?}
    BK -->|Successful| BL[Genome Integrity]
    BK -->|Residual Damage| BM[Secondary Repair]
    
    %% Quality Control
    BL --> BN[Normal DNA Structure]
    BN --> BO[Replication Competent]
    BO --> BP[Transcription Competent]
    BP --> BQ[Cell Survival]
    
    %% Error Pathways
    AD --> BR[Incomplete Repair]
    AP --> BR
    BE --> BR
    BM --> BS{Lesion Persistent?}
    BS -->|Yes| BT[Alternative Repair Pathways]
    BS -->|Bypass| BU[Translesion Synthesis]
    
    BT --> BV[Recombination Repair]
    BU --> BW[Error-Prone Bypass]
    
    %% Regulation and Coordination
    AX --> BY{Processing Type?}
    BY -->|3' Block| BZ(\1)
    BY -->|5' Block| CA(\1)
    BZ --> AV
    CA --> AV
    
    %% Final Outcomes
    BQ --> CB[Successful NER]
    BV --> CC[Backup Repair]
    BW --> CD[Mutagenic Outcome]

notes: Comprehensive model of E. coli nucleotide excision repair including both global genome and transcription-coupled sub-pathways. The UvrABC system is the bacterial paradigm for bulky lesion repair, structurally and mechanistically distinct from eukaryotic NER. Essential for publication as demonstrates complex multi-protein coordination with 4 AND gates and sophisticated damage recognition logic.
